trickyParts: In a browser worker ELK's bundled engine sees `self` and no `document`, takes the worker for an ELK worker and claims its onmessage, so every flowchart was refused ('En is not a constructor') in all three engines; beautiful-mermaid's `delete globalThis.self` does not reach WorkerGlobalScope.prototype's accessor. mermaid-render.worker.ts shadows `self` with an undefined accessor on the global's own prototype for the duration of each draw.
The 5 s clock starts when the worker posts {ready: true} (its imports loaded), not while its chunk downloads, so a slow connection never gets a normal diagram refused and cached.

Vite builds the worker as its own bundle; the third-party-notices plugin now records each worker bundle's files and inputs, leaves those files out of the page bundle check and adds their packages to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt.

Bundle at d9ff6c61: org.eclipse.elk only in mermaid-render.worker-*.js (1,565,608 B) and the lazy editor chunk lib-*.js (1,748,554 B); the entry and the headless chunks carry neither. Chromium worker timings: 50-edge flowchart 226/144 ms (first/warm), 100 nodes x2 edges ~1.2 s, 200 nodes ~3 s (5.4-5.7 s in WebKit/Firefox).

Browser harness: /legion/harness/setup.sh and env.sh; lanes by LEGION_ROLE (tester 20777, db dispatch_tester_e2e). web/dist was last built from the scratch negative-control commit: rebuild before any run.
